old: Only the security team can approve production firewall changes.
new: For the incident-response drill, the infrastructure team may approve firewall changes on the isolated test network.
note: The later decision applies only to an isolated test network during a drill, so it does not conflict with the production rule.

old: The marketing team may publish customer case studies only after legal approval.
new: Customer case studies require legal approval before publication.
note: The later statement expresses the same approval requirement without changing its substance.

old: The data platform runs scheduled ETL jobs at 02:00 UTC.
new: The reporting platform runs scheduled ETL jobs at 02:00 UTC.
note: The time and activity are identical, but the decisions concern different platforms.

old: Recruiting interviews for backend candidates require one coding round and one system-design round.
new: Recruiting interviews for backend candidates require one coding round, one system-design round, and an interview with the hiring manager.
note: The original two requirements are preserved and the later decision adds an additional interview requirement.

old: The checkout service retries failed payment requests three times and records each failure in the audit log.
new: The checkout service retries failed payment requests five times and records each failure in the audit log.
note: Both statements govern the same retry policy; the retry count has a different value while logging remains unchanged.

old: All engineering teams use Jira for sprint planning.
new: The developer-tools team uses Linear for sprint planning.
note: The later decision can be a team-specific exception without changing the planning tool used by the other engineering teams.

old: The finance team reviews expense reports every Friday.
new: The finance team reviews expense reports every Friday. Anika owns the review and posts the summary in the finance channel.
note: The review cadence is unchanged; the later statement only adds ownership and reporting details.

old: The API gateway accepts requests with a maximum payload of 5 MB.
new: The API gateway accepts requests with a maximum payload of 10 MB.
note: Both decisions define the same gateway-wide payload limit, but they specify different limits.

old: Design reviews happen asynchronously in the design channel.
new: Design reviews happen asynchronously in the design channel, with the product designer responsible for resolving unanswered comments.
note: The review method and location remain the same; the later statement adds responsibility for unresolved comments.

old: Customer refunds above $500 require finance approval.
new: Customer refunds above $1,000 require finance approval.
note: Both statements define the approval threshold for the same refund process, but the threshold is different.

old: The authentication service stores session data in DynamoDB.
new: The authentication service stores session data in Redis.
note: The same service and data type are involved, and the storage technology is different.

old: The sales team sends contract documents through DocuSign.
new: The legal team sends contract documents through DocuSign.
note: The statements concern different teams, so identical tooling does not make one decision a replacement for the other.

old: The incident channel is created automatically for severity-one incidents.
new: For the database migration exercise, the incident channel is created manually before the exercise begins.
note: The later statement concerns a specific exercise rather than the normal severity-one incident workflow.

old: Employees receive their equipment on their first day.
new: Employees receive their equipment on their first day, and workplace operations owns delivery tracking.
note: The delivery timing is unchanged and the later statement only adds the responsible team.

old: The search service indexes documents every six hours.
new: The search service indexes documents every hour.
note: Both statements define the same recurring indexing schedule for the same service.

old: The mobile app supports password-based login and Google login.
new: The mobile app supports password-based login and Apple login.
note: The two-part authentication decision retains password login but specifies a different social-login provider.

old: The office closes at 18:00 local time.
new: The office closes at 18:00 local time on weekdays; the support floor remains open until 22:00.
note: One reading treats the support-floor sentence as a scoped addition to the general office rule; another sees it as creating an exception to the closing time for part of the office.

old: All pull requests require two approvals before merging.
new: Pull requests created by the release automation bot require one approval before merging.
note: This can reasonably be read as a bot-specific exception to the two-approval rule, but it could also be treated as a conflicting merge policy for that class of pull request.

old: The customer dashboard displays billing and usage information.
new: The customer dashboard displays billing information; usage information is available in the analytics dashboard.
note: The later statement can be interpreted as moving usage information to another dashboard, but it could also describe an additional access path while leaving the original display intact.

old: The team uses the shared staging environment for integration testing.
new: The team uses a dedicated staging environment for payment integration testing.
note: The later decision may be a payment-specific environment exception, but without explicit scope it could also be read as replacing the team's staging environment choice.
